title: FinCEN (Treasury bureau) disclosed Tue Nov 24 unauthorized access to 'a limited subset of its systems', some taken offline as a precaution (alert read through The Verge, not at FinCEN); its order FIN-2026-R002 (read at fincen.gov) gives banks that batch-file by SDTM until Dec 30 for reports due Nov 18 to Dec 29
body:
# FinCEN cybersecurity incident

| Object | Read | Status |
|---|---|---|
| The incident | Unauthorized access to 'a limited subset of its systems'; some systems taken offline as a precaution; e-filing site works but 'some services may not be immediately available'; hotline unaffected | The Verge, Nov 25 01:00 UTC (page read), quoting FinCEN's alert; **the alert itself not read** (e-filing page is script-rendered) |
| The order | FIN-2026-R002, issued Nov 24: 'a service disruption that is hindering filers'; institutions that used SDTM as of Nov 18 file reports due Nov 18 to Dec 29 by **Dec 30**; same for beneficial ownership reports and FinCEN ID updates; other AML duties, monitoring included, stand; may be modified or extended | **primary, read at fincen.gov**. The order does not mention a cyber incident |
| SDTM outage | Alert on the e-filing site by Fri Nov 20 with no cause (JBizNews, through Sulat Nov 25) | secondary; FinCEN has not said the outage and the intrusion are one event |
| Not said | systems reached, data taken, start date, actor, any link to the CIA and ODNI breach reported the same day | The Verge: 'unclear if related' |

- **The bookmark overstates:** 'US Treasury hit by cyberattack, taking multiple FinCEN systems offline'. It is one bureau, and FinCEN took systems offline itself as a precaution. No department-wide event found.
- **So what:** no payment or settlement system is named. The money channel is (a) about six weeks of delayed batch suspicious-activity and currency reports from larger filers, and (b) if data left, bank-filed suspicious activity reports. Neither exposure is established. Delay in filing is a relief order, not a pause in monitoring.
- CYPHER owns the event; do not list institutions.
source: FinCEN order FIN-2026-R002 (fincen.gov PDF, read 2026-11-25T04:43Z) and FinCEN news list; The Verge 2026-11-25 01:00 UTC; Sulat 2026-11-25; Silicon Report Nov 24
confidence_language: order read at issuer; incident text through one press page; scope undisclosed
dispatch_note: PRIORITY. ACTION CYPHER. Channel info REGINALD, GIBBS (BSA filers), LIQUID (no payment system named). RED, PROME by BOARD diff.
route_summary: FinCEN intrusion; SDTM filing relief to Dec 30

title: CORRECTION of 20261124-018 item 8: the CIA and ODNI breach is reported, not 'no NYT story found'. The New York Times published it Nov 24; CyberScoop and Nextgov each confirmed it through unnamed sources: an unclassified open-source intelligence system, no classified network

| CIA declined to comment; ODNI did not respond | both pages. A search summary of another outlet says the agencies confirmed: not read, not carried |

- **So what:** no money channel found. CYPHER's federal-intrusion run (two at the FBI, one at the NSA per CyberScoop) gains one; a run is a count, not a common cause.

title: Releases missed by 011: Fed G.17 annual revision (Nov 24, read at federalreserve.gov): capacity utilization Q4 2025 76.5%, up 0.9 pt from the prior estimate, Oct 2026 industrial production level unchanged, 2025 growth revised DOWN half a point; German Ifo 90.6 (secondary); Australia October CPI 4.9% (ABS)
body:
# Releases, Nov 24 to 25

| Release | Print | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| Fed G.17 annual revision, Nov 24 | IP Oct 2026 +3.6% over the end of 2022, **unchanged**; growth 2023 and 2024 up about 0.5 pt a year, **2025 down 0.5 pt**; output 2023 to 2024 'little changed' (was a modest contraction) | Federal Reserve page, read |
| Same: capacity | capacity growth since 2022 averaged 1.0% a year (was 1.2%); **utilization Q4 2025 76.5%, +0.9 pt**, 2.9 pt under the 1972 to 2025 average; 2023 to 2025 up 0.8 pt on average | same |
| Same: composition | Dec 2022 to Oct 2026: durables +4.25% (0.75 pt less than before), nondurables +4% (0.75 pt more); base year 2022; Census AIES data for 2023 had more suppressed cells | same |
| German Ifo, November | 90.6 from 90.1 revised (consensus 90.5); conditions 89.4; expectations 91.9; seventh rise; Ifo president: the recovery 'lacks breadth' | RTE (Reuters), page read; ifo.de not read |
| Australia CPI, October | **4.9%** from 4.3%; month +0.5%; electricity +25.2% on rebates ending, automotive fuel +6.3% on the month | ABS release, read. Trimmed mean 3.8% from 3.6%: search summary |

- **ISHM:** any IP or utilization level a band uses is restated; re-base before grading. The upturn's level is the same, but its 2025 growth is smaller and durables carry less of it.
- **HANS:** Ifo is not a HANS-T row.
- Australia has no owner desk; info only.
